questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that the study destination had a vibrant city with lots of young people and a good  study environment. And that the city (and country) had an exciting and different culture that I wanted to explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a very good experience and I meet so many nice people from all over the world and had some great experiences, and learned a lot about the culture. However, covid still had its influence and most of my lectures were online and therefore I was not present at the university as much as I wanted to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to get the information from the host university and they were very helpful if I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received different emails about how to enroll classes and orientation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing in the city. As an exchange student I could not get housing through the university because full-time students were prioritised, and there were very limited options in the city compared to how many students were searching for accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Search for accommodation as soon as possible

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was too difficult to get housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recall it as an easy process were i just needed to fill out some forms online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I felt like I could always email the university administration but I did not have the need for it in this process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of 3 of the classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to ask the course administrators if you have any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the courses that I took were very exciting and I learned a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 4 classes and I think the level was pretty much like the university of Copenhagen,

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had seminars in every course every week where it was mostly discussions in smaller groups and in the whole class, which is different from Copenhagen were it is mostly lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Crime, Violence and Social Control in Africa
Ways of Living: Studying Different Worlds
Migration, Settlement and Belonging

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked all my courses but i think especially Migration, Settlement and Belonging was really interesting and very good professors.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on different trips, for example to the Isle of Skye which was about 1500 DKK but worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think everything was like I expected. A bit expensive accommodation but food, coffee, restaurants etc is a little bit cheaper than copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there were a lot of nice options to do sports or join other clubs! But I lived in another part of the city than the university and therefore I didnt join any sport clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many different clubs that I dont even know what you could not join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would have loved to be a part of one of the sport clubs which I would definitely have been if I lived nearer the university!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands on a hike, go to a football match, The Isle of Skye, visit other cities (fx Edinburgh, Stirling, St Andrews)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Scottish people are so nice and welcoming!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was a little difficult to meet the local students mostly because the majority of students in my classes were international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the kindness and hospitality!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun and enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Mostly just to ask the university administration if you have any questions. They are really helpful so dont hesitate to ask for help

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To make friends with people from all over the world!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge was to keep up with the covid restrictions, test system and so on in another country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
